papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background.  Protein Mendelian randomization (MR) is now routine, and a common inference treats an estimate built from a ligand's own cis protein quantitative trait locus (pQTL) and one built from its receptor's as evidence about the same pathway. That assumption has not been tested since it means comparing MR estimates across a network of interacting proteins, and network comparisons violate the independence that standard multiple-testing corrections assume. Methods.  Using cis-pQTLs as instruments, we analyzed 660 of the 661 UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project proteins spanning 1,129 curated ligand–receptor pairs, and estimated effects on coronary artery disease in two genome-wide association studies (GWAS): Nikpay 2015 (60,801 cases, no UK Biobank overlap) and Aragam 2022 (181,522 cases, which include the Nikpay data). Discordance between ligand-level and receptor-level estimates was tested against a permutation null holding every protein's estimate and degree fixed and randomizing only the pairing. Estimates were followed up with Bayesian colocalization and with replication on a second proteomic platform. Results.  Ligand and receptor estimates agreed no more than randomly paired proteins: 48.5% same-direction against a rewired null of 49.8% (p = 0.64) in Nikpay, and 47.0% against 50.0% (p = 0.20) in Aragam. Counts of significantly discordant pairs rose threefold with outcome power, from 10 to 31, and the null rose with them, from 9 to 30 (p = 0.85). Bonferroni correction across 476 deduplicated pairs built from 361 proteins reported ten discoveries that three proteins account for. A node-shuffling null gave p = 0.014 because protein degree correlates with effect size in Aragam (rho = + 0.133, p = 0.008). Flagging protein-altering instruments, a routine sensitivity analysis, flagged PCSK9 and showed no enrichment among causal proteins (Fisher p ≥ 0.44). Colocalization verdicts survived a change of outcome GWAS at only 11 of 14 loci (PP.H4 ≥ 0.8), mostly through outcome power; one locus reversed outright. Conclusions.  Ligand-level and receptor-level MR are not interchangeable evidence about a pathway. More important, the naive analysis that appears to identify specific discordant pairs is reproducible. It returns ten pairs after correction, headed by one at p = 8.5 × 10  − 7  , and we show what removes them.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Transcriptome-wide Mendelian randomization (MR) can identify expression traits associated with disease, but correlated cis-regulation may cause multiple neighboring traits to reflect the same underlying locus. We investigated chronic kidney disease (CKD) using a locus-aware framework that interpreted genetically connected expression traits at the locus level rather than as independent gene-level findings. Methods  We tested 15,285 blood cis-eQTL-defined expression traits for association with CKD in FinnGen. Single-instrument traits were analyzed using the Wald ratio, while traits with multiple instruments were analyzed using multiplicative random-effects inverse-variance weighted MR (MRE-IVW). Traits meeting the FDR threshold underwent locus mapping, colocalization, assessment in an independent CKD dataset, and integration of renal transcriptomic, kidney eQTL, and single-nucleus evidence. Results  The primary analysis identified 28 FDR-significant gene-expression traits, 12 of which also met the Bonferroni threshold. These traits were grouped into nine operationally defined candidate loci, with 19 mapping to a single complex locus within the major histocompatibility complex (MHC). Strong colocalization was observed for  ANKUB1  and  RSAD2  at distinct non-MHC loci and for  IER3  within the MHC. After excluding the MHC, nine FDR-significant traits remained across eight non-MHC loci, including two Bonferroni-significant traits and two with strong colocalization. Among the five traits eligible for multi-instrument sensitivity analyses, none showed a significant MR-Egger intercept. One TUBB leave-one-out omission met the prespecified influence criterion. In the primary exact-rsID CKDGen analysis, 14 traits were estimable and 11 showed direction-concordant effects, although none remained significant after replication-wide FDR correction. Identifier harmonization enabled all 28 traits to be evaluated and identified four FDR-significant, direction-concordant traits, all within the MHC. These findings strengthened support for the MHC locus without resolving gene attribution within the region. Conclusions  Transcriptome-wide MR identified 28 CKD-associated expression traits across nine candidate loci.  ANKUB1  and  RSAD2  were prioritized as distinct non-MHC candidates with strong colocalization support by colocalization, whereas  IER3  remained embedded within an unresolved complex MHC locus despite strong single-signal colocalization. These findings support targeted functional follow-up without establishing any candidate as a validated causal gene or therapeutic target.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Which candidates are phenotyped largely decides the accuracy of genomic prediction, yet few programmes design training sets formally. papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Which candidates are phenotyped largely decides the accuracy of genomic prediction, yet few programmes design training sets formally. Existing tools evaluate the design criterion, the mean generalised coefficient of determination (CDmean), in a reduced marker space or repeatedly inside stochastic searches, optimise for one assumed heritability, and offer little built-in support for multi-environment trials or historical records. TSOpt removes these limits. It updates the exact CDmean by rank-one steps, so a design for several hundred lines takes about 0.1 s, averages the criterion over the unknown heritability, and uses one engine for line × environment and line × trait units, lines already phenotyped, hybrids, plot costs and major genes. We tested it on 328 elite lines from eight seasons of the International Rice Research Institute’s irrigated breeding programme. Twenty-five TSOpt lines predicted untested lines as accurately as 76–167 random lines. TSOpt raised predictive ability over random sampling by 0.097 (95% confidence interval 0.045–0.150), was ahead of STPGA on average, and ran at least 900 times faster. With a quarter of line × season combinations tested over four seasons, its sparse-testing allocations predicted untested combinations better than balanced random allocation, even when scored with correlations unseen by the design; with half tested, it did not. Forward in time, all design methods gained little and the full history remained the best training set. On six public panels TSOpt matched STPGA, TSDFGS and published TrainSel designs, much faster. Lines with the highest mean relationship to the targets never beat random choice.

papers.abstract_full: Spatial heterogeneity is a major source of environmental noise in field trials, reducing genetic evaluation accuracy. Conventional spatial correction methods use field layout and plot proximity but often fail to capture in-season dynamics or leverage temporal data from high-throughput phenotyping. We hypothesized that longitudinal UAV-derived multispectral measurements could characterize field-scale environmental heterogeneity and improve genetic evaluation in breeding trials. Multispectral imagery was collected throughout the growing season across eight alfalfa trials in New York and New Mexico (2022–2023). Vegetation indices were evaluated for heritability and association with biomass yield using univariate and multi-trait models. Longitudinal measurements were modeled with random regression (RR) to estimate plot-specific permanent environmental effects (PEE), incorporated into genomic mixed models within a two-stage framework. Model performance was compared with conventional autoregressive (AR) and baseline (no correction) models using metrics of consistency and accuracy of estimated genetic effects across replicates. Vegetation indices showed moderate to high heritability, with GNDVI consistently outperforming NDVI and NDRE. Both univariate and multi-trait analyses revealed substantial spatial variability, particularly in New Mexico trials. RR-derived PEE captured field-scale spatial patterns and improved genetic signal recovery relative to baseline and AR models, with the largest gains under strong spatial heterogeneity and comparable performance where variability was limited. The RR framework improved reproducibility of genetic effect estimates across independent field subsets without compromising agreement with full-trial evaluations. These findings show that integrating UAV data via random regression enhances genetic signal recovery and selection accuracy, with broader potential for precision agriculture and biosensor-driven crop management.

papers.abstract_full: Root anatomy plays a critical role in water and nutrients acquisition and influences plant adaptation to abiotic stresses. A better understanding of the genetic control of anatomical traits is important to improve rice production, a staple crop for half of the world’s population. In this study, we measured eleven root anatomical traits in a collection of 185 Vietnamese rice landraces, and conducted genome-wide association studies to uncover the genetic architecture underlying these traits. A total of 24 significant small nucleotide polymorphisms were identified, corresponding to 19 quantitative trait loci for traits such as root cross section area, cortex area, metaxylem area or theoretical axial conductance. Interestingly, several root anatomical traits correlated with previously characterized root architectural traits measured within the same Vietnamese rice collection, and some genetic regions associated with anatomical traits and drought-tolerance-related traits colocalized. Candidate genes potentially involved in root development and cell wall patterning were identified within these QTLs regions. In particular, the significant SNP in qRA10.1 associated with metaxylem area induces an amino-acid change in the kinase domain of a wall associated kinase (WAK) receptor-like protein kinase (OsWAK111) with an extracellular epidermal growth factor (EGT)-containing domain that bind pectin, which presumably sense perturbations in this component to influence cell elongation during plant development. This study reveal key determinants of the genetic control of root anatomy in rice, which could be exploited to enhance tolerance to abiotic stresses such as drought.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background:  Androgen receptor (AR)-positive triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) represents a distinct molecular subtype driven by androgen signaling. However, existing clinical evidence is largely limited to small, early-phase single-arm trials with inconsistent endpoint definitions. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the clinical activity and safety profile of AR pathway-targeted therapies in patients with AR-positive TNBC. Methods: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and ClinicalTrials.gov were systematically searched from database inception through February 2026. Quantitative synthesis focused on patients with advanced or metastatic disease, using a random-effects generalized linear mixed model to pool objective response rates (ORR) and clinical benefit rates (CBR) at standardized timepoints (16 weeks and 6 months). Neoadjuvant studies were evaluated qualitatively. Results: Eleven studies met inclusion criteria (10 in advanced/metastatic settings, 1 neoadjuvant). Across nine advanced-disease studies (296 patients), the pooled ORR was 5.4% (95% CI: 3.3%–8.6%; I  2   = 0.0%). Standardized CBR was 30.7% (95% CI: 24.3%–37.9%) at 16 weeks (176 patients across 5 studies) and 19.6% (95% CI: 11.2%–32.1%) at 6 months (56 patients across 2 studies). In the neoadjuvant setting, 16.7% of patients achieved a pathological complete response. Safety outcomes were synthesized narratively due to varied reporting definitions. Conclusion: AR pathway-targeted therapies demonstrate limited direct tumor shrinkage but achieve durable disease control in nearly one-third of patients at standardized intervals. Given the reliance on small single-arm trials with varying AR positivity cutoffs, these findings represent signals of clinical activity rather than direct proof of superiority over standard treatments.

papers.abstract_full: Aim:  The Oral Frailty Diet (OF Diet) has been implemented since 2022 as a safe initial meal option for elderly patients on emergency admission, addressing risks of malnutrition,dysphagia, choking, and aspiration. However, the prevalence of oral frailty and dysphagia among elderly emergency admissions is unclear, and the suitability of the OF Diet against patients’ actual swallowing abilities has not been systematically assessed. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate the impact the OF Diet on swallowing function and dietary intake in elderly patients (≥70 years) on emergency admission. Methods: This retrospective study included 478 patients aged ≥70 years on emergency admission between October 2022 and December 2024. Patients were divided into OF Diet (n=108) and non-OF Diet (n=370) groups. Assessments included meal texture at admission and after modification, swallowing function (Seirei Swallowing Questionnaire), and dietary intake. Results: Initial meal provision comprised 53% regular diet and 23% OF Diet. The OF Diet group had a higher rate of suspected dysphagia on admission (p&lt;0.0001). While the non-OF Diet group showed significant deterioration in meal texture from admission to modification (p&lt;0.0001), the OF Diet group showed stable textures. A linear mixed model revealed significant main effects of the OF Diet (F=19.71, p&lt;0.0001) on swallowing scores. The OF Diet group also demonstrated significantly lower dietary intake &lt;30% (12.0% vs. 21.4%, p=0.0308). Conclusions: Implementation of the OF Diet enables safe initial meal provision for elderly patients on emergency admission who are at high risk of dysphagia, thereby improving dietary intake without negatively affecting swallowing function.

papers.abstract_full: This study investigates the benefits for rainbow trout selective breeding of using triploid performances rather than diploid ones. Its objectives were to estimate genetic parameters, assess genetic correlations between ploidy levels, and evaluate the gain in selection efficiency using triploid sib testing. The traits analysed were growth, carcass traits, fat content, and acute hypoxia tolerance using pedigree-based and genomic models. Results showed that diploids were heavier and longer than triploids at slaughter age. Triploids exhibited greater tolerance to acute hypoxia in this experiment, although the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. However, heritability estimates for most traits were similar between ploidy levels when genetic models correctly accounted for triploidy and the unequal maternal and paternal chromosome contributions. Incorrectly treating triploids as diploids substantially overestimated genetic variance and heritability values. Genetic correlations between diploid and triploid performances were high for all traits but varied from 0.60 to 0.98. Correlations were particularly high for carcass yield, fat-related traits and hypoxia tolerance indicating that selection based on diploid performance can efficiently improve these characteristics in triploid offspring. Conversely, correlations for body weight and length were lower, suggesting that evaluating triploid relatives could improve selection accuracy for growth. Overall, the findings support diploid-based selection as an effective strategy for improving triploid production traits, particularly carcass yield and flesh quality. Direct evaluation of triploid relatives may provide additional benefits for growth-related traits. The study highlights the importance of appropriate genetic and genomic models and recommends assessing the economic value of triploid performance testing for each target trait.

papers.abstract: Abstract  Translating genetic risk for complex traits into mechanistic insight requires locating risk signals within native tissue architectures. papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Translating genetic risk for complex traits into mechanistic insight requires locating risk signals within native tissue architectures. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) provides high-resolution anatomical context, its integration with genome-wide association studies (GWAS) can be confounded by linkage disequilibrium (LD) and spatial autocorrelation. These factors can generate spurious associations and spread localized genetic signals across non-specific tissue regions. Here we establish a genotype-aware spatial simulation benchmark and develop SDESE (Spatially refined Driver Estimation by Selective Expression), a framework for joint spatial and gene fine-mapping of complex phenotypes. SDESE couples spatial localization with gene prioritization through iterative conditional association analysis, thereby reducing signals attributable to LD proxies and co-expression. We also provide a multi-organ spatial resource and analysis platform for downstream applications. In spatial simulations, SDESE retained high sensitivity while reducing non-specific spatial spread, particularly for localized signals. We then applied SDESE to adult human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) ST data from five common psychiatric disorders and validated the results using multiple independent GWAS datasets. Genetic risk across these disorders converged on shared neuroanatomical niches, particularly mid-to-deep cortical layers and excitatory neuronal microenvironments. However, the corresponding associated-gene sets showed limited overlap, while functional enrichment implicated neurodevelopmental, synaptic and ion-transport processes across disorders. These findings reveal a layered spatial-genetic architecture in which shared neuroanatomical vulnerability coexists with partially distinct but functionally convergent sets of associated genes.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Metabolic dysregulation has been implicated in Alzheimer disease (AD) and Parkinson disease (PD), yet circulating metabolites are embedded within highly correlated metabolic networks. This structure complicates single-metabolite analyses and motivates genetic approaches that model shared metabolic architecture directly. Methods  We applied Genomic SEM to NMR metabolite GWAS summary statistics to construct lipid and non-lipid latent metabolic factor GWAS. Six factors were screened against AD, PD, and Lewy body dementia using cross-trait LDSC, followed by MiXeR, pleiotropy-informed locus discovery, colocalization, transcriptomic prioritization, single-cell projection, virtual knockout, and target annotation. Results  Among 18 factor-disease comparisons, three survived FDR correction: an HDL-core axis positively correlated with AD (rg = 0.142, FDR = 0.002), a ketone-body axis inversely correlated with PD (rg = -0.106, FDR = 0.015), and a TG-rich/VLDL-remodeling axis inversely correlated with PD (rg = -0.072, FDR = 0.031). Component-level LDSC supported the biological traceability of these axes. Downstream analyses linked HDL-core/AD to perivascular support, ketone-body/PD to distributed neuronal-glial energy adaptation, and TG/VLDL-remodeling/PD to lysosomal and membrane-trafficking programs. Target annotation prioritized experimentally approachable genes including  GRK4  ,  PRMT7  , and  TMEM175  . Conclusions  Structured metabolic genetic axes reveal selective and biologically distinct links between circulating metabolism and neurodegenerative disease, providing a framework for mechanism-focused follow-up beyond single-metabolite association.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract  Introduction:  Psychiatric disorders show substantial genetic overlap, but the mechanisms underlying this shared liability remain poorly understood. Biobehavioral traits such as neuroticism and cognitive ability are heritable and genetically correlated with multiple psychiatric disorders, and may contribute to shared genetic risk. We investigated whether these traits account for genetic correlations among nine major psychiatric disorders; anorexia nervosa, anxiety, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder, autism spectrum disorder, bipolar disorder, depression, obsessive-compulsive disorder, post-traumatic stress disorder and schizophrenia. Methods  We analysed summary statistics from the largest available genome-wide association study (GWAS) of these nine psychiatric disorders, two neuroticism subtypes (‘depressed affect’ and ‘worry’) and four cognitive measures (verbal-numerical reasoning, reaction time, memory and educational attainment). Genomic Structural Equation Modelling was used to determine whether biobehavioural traits influenced pairwise genetic correlations between psychiatric disorders. Results  Accounting for a biobehavioural trait significantly altered genetic correlations between 54 of 168 pairs of psychiatric disorders (32%). The neuroticism dimension of ‘worry’ produced the largest average change and, in some cases, almost completely accounted for genetic correlation between psychiatric disorders, such as between depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder. Educational attainment accounted for the greatest number of significant changes overall, indicating a broad contribution to shared genetic risk across psychiatric disorders. Conclusions  The transdiagnostic biobehavioural traits neuroticism and cognitive ability partially explain genetic overlap between psychiatric disorders in this study, although effects vary across traits and disorders. This heterogeneity highlights distinct biological pathways underlying psychiatric comorbidity and may inform psychiatric classification, future genetic studies, and transdiagnostic intervention strategies.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Medical student research productivity has become an increasingly visible signal in plastic surgery residency selection, yet the extent to which students have transitioned from contributors to first authors within the specialty literature remains unclear. We evaluated temporal trends, authorship structure, and institutional concentration of medical student authorship in plastic surgery publications. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional analysis of U.S.-affiliated articles published in Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery, PRS Global Open, and Annals of Plastic Surgery from 2010 through 2025. An AI-enabled extraction pipeline identified author credentials, authorship position, institutional affiliation, publication year, and team size. Medical students were classified by bachelor-level credentials without concurrent doctoral-level degrees. Temporal trends in medical student first authorship were evaluated using segmented regression with a prespecified 2018 breakpoint. RESULTS: Among 13,723 eligible publications, 4227 (30.8%) included at least one medical student author and 2135 (15.6%) were first-authored by a medical student. Medical student first authorship increased from 58 publications in 2010 (9.5%) to 209 in 2025 (20.9%), peaking at 24.3% in 2022. Mean annual first-author output increased by 143% between the early and late eras (77.8 versus 189.1 publications/year). Segmented regression demonstrated significant post-2018 slope acceleration (P<0.001). Publications with medical student authors had larger teams than those without student involvement (mean, 6.14 versus 4.01 authors; P<0.001). The top 20 institutions accounted for 53.0% of identifiable student first-author publications. CONCLUSIONS: Medical student authorship in plastic surgery has undergone marked temporal acceleration, with increasing first-author leadership embedded within larger collaborative teams. Student first authorship may signal merit, but also reflects access to mentorship, infrastructure, and institutional research opportunity.

OBJECTIVE: To assess national trends in psychiatry residency fill rates in France and examine the territorial distribution of unfilled positions from 2016-2017 to 2025-2026. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective longitudinal panel study including all 28 French residency subdivisions over 10 academic years. Opened a…
papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Mental health needs are increasing across Europe, while psychiatric workforce planning in France is challenged by workforce ageing and territorial inequalities. OBJECTIVE: To assess national trends in psychiatry residency fill rates in France and examine the territorial distribution of unfilled positions from 2016-2017 to 2025-2026. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective longitudinal panel study including all 28 French residency subdivisions over 10 academic years. Opened and filled positions were extracted from decrees published in the French Official Journal. Fill rates were modelled using a beta-binomial generalised linear mixed model. Heterogeneity was quantified using the median odds ratio, and concentration using the Gini coefficient and top-share estimates. RESULTS: The panel included 280 subdivision-year observations, corresponding to 5282 opened, 4719 filled, and 563 unfilled positions. Observed national fill rates declined from near-complete levels before 2019 to 82.49% in 2019-2020 and remained below pre-2019 levels thereafter. The model-based national fill rate decreased from 98.10% in the early period to 82.74% in the late period, an absolute change of -15.4 percentage points. Between-subdivision heterogeneity was substantial. Unfilled positions were territorially concentrated and the top 25% of subdivisions accounted for 61.3% of all unfilled positions. CONCLUSIONS: Psychiatry residency underfilling in France has become a sustained, territorially uneven workforce planning issue. In centralised rank-based allocation systems, workforce planning should monitor not only the number of training positions opened, but also their conversion into filled positions and the territorial accumulation of vacancies.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Neurodegeneration drives irreversible disability in multiple sclerosis (MS). Ferroptosis has been implicated in MS and experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE), but its spatiotemporal dynamics and imaging correlates remain unclear. METHODS: We combined 7.0 T diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) with histopathological and molecular analyses to evaluate the effects of Liproxstatin-1 (Lip-1) in mice with EAE induced by myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein peptide 35-55 (MOG35-55). Sixty-four female C57BL/6 mice were assigned to control, EAE, early-treatment (Early-Tx; Lip-1 from day 12), and late-treatment (Late-Tx; Lip-1 from day 18) groups. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and tissue analyses were performed at days 20 and 30 post-immunization. RESULTS: Early-Tx reduced clinical severity at day 30 (vs. EAE; p < 0.001) and limited body weight loss. At peak disease, voxel- and ROI-based DTI showed increased mean diffusivity and radial diffusivity in the corpus callosum, internal capsule, and thalamus, which were attenuated by Early-Tx. At the chronic stage, EAE showed persistent fractional anisotropy reduction in periventricular white matter and corpus callosum, whereas Early-Tx largely prevented these abnormalities. Histology demonstrated that Early-Tx suppressed inflammatory infiltration, microglial activation, and demyelination while preserving myelin integrity. Acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 4 (ACSL4) upregulation and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation preceded overt iron deposition, whereas iron accumulation emerged mainly at the chronic stage and colocalized with activated microglia and demyelinated lesions. CONCLUSIONS: Ferroptosis-related molecular alterations are associated with stage-dependent inflammatory demyelinating injury in EAE. Early Lip-1 treatment provides greater microstructural protection than delayed treatment. High-field DTI sensitively detects treatment-responsive microstructural injury and may help monitor ferroptosis-related pathology in demyelinating disease.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Hyperkalemia is common in dehydrated calves with neonatal diarrhea and can result in life-threatening cardiac conduction abnormalities. HYPOTHESIS/OBJECTIVES: Compare the effects of IV small-volume hypertonic solutions of NaHCO3, NaCl, and glucose in correcting electrocardiographic abnormalities. ANIMALS: Twenty-two neonatal diarrheic calves with plasma potassium concentrations (cK) > 5.8 mmol/L. METHODS: Prospective randomized clinical trial. Calves randomly received either 8.4% NaHCO3 (6.4 mL/kg; n = 7), 7.5% NaCl (5 mL/kg; n = 8), or 46.2% glucose (5 mL/kg; n = 7) IV over 5 min and were subsequently allowed to suckle 2 L of an oral electrolyte solution. Lead II ECG variables were determined before the infusion, during infusion, and 7, 15, 30, 60, 90, and 120 min after the start of infusion. RESULTS: Seven minutes after initiation of infusions, administration of hypertonic sodium solutions but not glucose resulted in a significant (P < .05) increase in heart rate and ST segment duration as well as a decrease in heart rate variability, QRS duration, and T wave amplitude. Generalized linear mixed model analysis identified cK, the interaction between cK and plasma sodium concentrations, or both, as significant predictors of most electrocardiographic variables. Posttreatment increase in cK in 2 calves in group NaCl was associated with the loss of P waves, prolonged QRS duration, and increased T wave amplitude. CONCLUSIONS AND CLINICAL IMPORTANCE: Hypertonic sodium solutions allow for a rapid reversal of the cardiotoxic effect of hyperkalemia. Hypertonic NaHCO3 should be preferred over hypertonic NaCl or glucose.

papers.abstract_full: INTRODUCTION: Genotype × environment interaction (G×E) complicates the identification of high-yielding and stable cowpea genotypes across variable production environments. This study evaluated 20 advanced cowpea breeding lines for grain yield, stability, and multi-trait performance across five location-year environments in Ghana during the 2024 and 2025 cropping seasons. METHODS: Trials were conducted using a randomized complete block design with three replications. Both seasons were drought-prone, although moisture stress varied among location-year environments because of erratic rainfall distribution. Grain yield was analysed using additive main effects and multiplicative interaction (AMMI) and genotype plus genotype × environment (GGE) biplot analyses, while grain yield, biomass yield, harvest index, hundred-seed weight, and days to 95% pod maturity were integrated using the Multi-Trait Stability Index (MTSI). RESULTS: Analysis of variance revealed significant (p < 0.001) effects of environment, genotype, and G×E. The first two interaction principal components explained 92.15% of G×E variation, with Wa_2025 showing the largest IPCA1 score. Tuzievallenga had the highest mean grain yield (1149 kg ha-1), whereas IT17K-2030-2 had the lowest AMMI Stability Value (ASV = 114.54). Five genotypes combined high yield with relative stability: Tuzievallenga, IT17K-2030-2, IT17K-1095-2-2, IT17K-849-2-1, and IT17K-1802-1. MTSI values ranged from 2.035 to 5.518, with IT17K-1095-2-2, IT17K-849-2-1, IT17K-1403-1-1, IT17K-2024-4, and Tuzievallenga having the lowest values. IT17K-1095-2-2, IT17K-849-2-1, and Tuzievallenga were common to the top five selections from both approaches. GGE identified one common sector comprising Damongo_2024, Manga_2025, and Nyankpala_2024, with Tuzievallenga as the winning genotype, while Wa_2025 and Nyankpala_2025 formed distinct sectors associated with SARI-tuya and IT17K-1266-2-1, respectively. DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: The findings demonstrate substantial G×E differentiation and identify promising genotypes for farmer-managed on-farm evaluation and complementary use in cowpea breeding.

papers.abstract_full: Background  Commercial spaceflight now carries civilians on short missions, yet their stress-axis physiology is poorly described. Earlier shuttle data suggest that sympathetic responses predominate after short flights and glucocorticoid responses after long ones. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) is a low-cost readout of both. Methods  Preregistered secondary analysis of open clinical laboratory data (NASA Open Science Data Repository OSD-569 and OSD-575) from the four Inspiration4 crew members, each sampled seven times: three draws before launch, one the day after return (R+1) and three during recovery (R+45 to R+194). Log-transformed NLR was modelled with a linear mixed model with a random intercept per crew member and Kenward-Roger inference. Lymphocyte and eosinophil counts and C-reactive protein were secondary outcomes with false discovery rate correction. Results  All 28 draws were analysed. NLR at R+1 did not differ from pre-flight (fold change 1.04; 95% CI 0.81 to 1.34; p = 0.73); two crew members increased (+25% and +46%) and two decreased (−27% and−11%). During recovery NLR was 23% lower than pre-flight (fold change 0.77; 95% CI 0.64 to 0.92; p = 0.005). No secondary outcome changed after correction; lymphocytes were 18% lower at R+1 (95% CI −35% to +4%; q = 0.31). Between-person differences explained 58% of the variance. An ordinary regression ignoring repeated measures missed the recovery effect (p = 0.08). Conclusions  A 3-day orbital flight produced no consistent leukocyte stress signature one day after return. The lower NLR during recovery suggests that pre-flight values, not recovery values, deviate from the resting state, which has implications for how baselines are defined in short-duration spaceflight studies.

papers.abstract_full: Functional data are widely collected across many fields. One approach for modeling functional data collected across repeated measures is longitudinal functional PCA (LFPCA), which allows for the decomposition of variability at multiple levels. However, existing estimation approaches for LFPCA can be computationally demanding for large or high-dimensional datasets. Here, we propose fast generalized LFPCA, a novel estimation technique that bins data along the functional domain and fits a marginal mixed model at each bin. Simulation results show that the proposed method is orders of magnitude faster than existing techniques while achieving similar accuracy, making LFPCA scalable to datasets with more densely sampled observations and larger sample sizes. We apply the proposed technique to model neuronal firing rate data both on and off deep brain stimulation (DBS) to investigate how the intervention modulates populationlevel neuronal activity. Our results suggest that the vast majority of between-neuron variation can be explained by four principal components, which relate to individual differences in neuronal firing as well as the arm manipulation paradigm under study. We also find that DBS significantly increases the variability of firing activity, likely driven by increased firing from a subset of neurons in response to DBS, a novel insight not obtained in previous analyses. Code to implement the proposed method and run simulation studies is included in the supplement.

papers.abstract_full: Bipolar disorder (BD) is a highly heritable psychiatric disorder. An increasing number of whole-exome sequencing (WES) studies have been conducted on psychiatric research. However, few studies have investigated the association between single nucleotide variants (SNVs) in WES and structural brain changes in patients with BD. We conducted WES on 93 patients with BD and 161 healthy controls (HCs) to detect germline variants and copy number alterations (CNAs), as well as the gene-based effects of rare variants on BD. The impact of genetic factors on structural neuroimaging markers, including cortical thickness and white matter tract integrity, was examined using neuroimaging-genetic association analysis. We identified 382 BD-related genes, including SYNE1, PKHD1L1, FRAS1, and ZFHX4, from a systematic review, and the most frequently mutated genes. We identified a new gene, GNB3, which harbors a significant burden of rare nonsynonymous variants that affect BD. By integrating WES and structural neuroimaging data, we found that the single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs56850341 in KMT2C was substantially correlated with structural neuroimaging measures, including cortical thickness and white matter tract integrity. In the present study, we suggest that rare nonsynonymous variants in GNB3 may be involved in the pathophysiology of BD, and that highly contributing heritable genetic variant in KMT2C may influence brain structural changes.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: To evaluate trends in psychotropic prescription rates (PRs) in a Peruvian general hospital during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted an interrupted time-series (ITS) study using routinely collected clinical data from hospitalized patients with psychiatric diagnoses between September 2020 and December 2024. Psychotropic PRs, defined as the number of weekly psychotropic prescriptions per 1,000 psychiatric consultations, were calculated overall and by subclass: antidepressants (N06A), antipsychotics (N05A), anxiolytics (N05B), and mood stabilizers (N05AN01/N03A). For ITS analysis, the study period was divided into six predefined phases (two waves, three relaxation phases, and one post-pandemic phase) based on COVID-19 mortality and transmission trends in Peru. Segmented regression models were applied to estimate phase-specific level and slope changes. RESULTS: A total of 6,151 patients were included. The overall psychotropic PR was higher during the post-pandemic period compared with the pandemic period (1,308 vs. 1,254; p = 0.023). ITS analyses showed a significant downward trend in overall psychotropic prescribing during phase 1 (post-first wave stabilization, β = -25.53; 95% CI = -43.82 to -7.01; p = 0.007), followed by a structural break in phase 2 (second pandemic wave) with an abrupt level increase (β = 295.53; 95% CI = 60.48 to 530.57; p = 0.014) and slope reversal (β = 23.79; 95% CI = 3.33 to 44.26; p = 0.016), after which prescribing stabilized. A similar temporal pattern was observed for antidepressant PR. Anxiolytic PR displayed a transient upward slope change in phase 2 (β = 14.15; 95% CI = 1.80 to 26.50; p = 0.01), whereas antipsychotic and mood stabilizer prescribing remained stable across phases. CONCLUSIONS: Overall psychotropic prescribing showed phase-specific disruption followed by structural rebound and subsequent stabilization across the COVID-19 and post-pandemic periods. These findings provide real-world evidence and underscore the need to monitor psychiatric prescribing and mental health service adaptation in middle-income settings.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Bipolar disorder (BD) manifests both genetic predispositions and brain imaging abnormalities. Genetic analyses provide a powerful approach to disentangling the associations between BD and brain imaging-derived phenotype (IDP). However, in East Asian (EAS) populations, the genetic basis of these neuroimaging changes and their clinical relevance remains underexplored due to limited integrative evidence. METHODS: We investigated the genetic architecture and clinical relevance of BD and brain IDPs in East Asian populations using individual-level data from the Chinese Bipolar Disorder (CN-BD) cohort (N = 3,920), summary statistics of BD from the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium (PGC) (N = 16,915) and of IDPs from the CHIMGEN Consortium (N = 7,058), and genotype and clinical data from the Chinese Longitudinal and Systematic Study of Bipolar Disorder cohort (CLASS-BD). We employed genetic correlation (GNOVA), multi-trait meta-analysis (MTAG, CPASSOC), and ancestry-specific fine-mapping (MESuSiE) to identify shared genetic loci. Functional annotation, protein association (SMR, BLISS), and spatiotemporal expression trajectory analyses were conducted. Bidirectional Mendelian Randomization (MR) assessed causal relationships, and polygenic risk score (PRS)-PheWAS explored phenome-level associations with clinical traits. RESULTS: Our multi-trait meta-analysis identified 11 pleiotropic single nucleotide variants (SNVs) implicated in BD-IDP pairs, showing convergent enrichment in lipid metabolism and neurotransmitter biosynthesis pathways. Fine-mapping revealed an EAS-specific causal signal (rs7941324 near RPS27P20), which demonstrated high posterior inclusion probability in EAS but not European ancestries, and colocalized with BD and specific brain alterations. MR revealed 27 IDP-to-BD and 35 BD-to-IDP causal relationships, distinguishing structural changes of the parietal and temporal gyri as markers preceding BD onset and the right precuneus area as a state marker that followed BD onset. Clinically, BD-IDP polygenic risk scores were significantly associated with depressive symptoms, anxiety, and suicide risk. Mediation analysis further indicated that depressive and anxiety symptoms statistically mediated the relationship between BD-IDP PRS and suicide risk. Moreover, PRS-PheWAS identified 135 significant associations with metabolic phenotypes, highlighting a psycho-metabolic nexus in BD. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings reveal associations between polygenicity and distinct BD brain patterns and clinical profiles. We identified ancestry-specific causal variants and bidirectional BD-IDP relationships. PRS associations with depressive symptoms, anxiety, suicide risk, and metabolic phenotypes highlight precision medicine potential for BD.

papers.abstract_full: When trihydroxypiperidine (PIP) or DAB-1 pyrrolidine (PYR) iminosugars are multimerized on the prism[5]arene scaffold, they generate highly efficient multivalent inhibitors of GCase. Binding trihydroxypiperidine to the rims of prism[5]arene (PrS[5]PIP) results in a multivalent derivative that is more effective than others reported in the literature with the same bioactive unit. This efficacy is attributed to the role of prism[5]arene, whose barrel-like shape exposes an external π-surface that enables van der Waals contacts and other secondary interactions with the enzyme, thereby enhancing affinity for GCase through dimer stabilization. The high efficiency of PrS[5]PIP is supported by in silico calculations that showed how the crowding of the bioactive units on the rims of the macrocycle promotes a rearrangement allowing the active site to accommodate two trihydroxypiperidine units, which engage in hydrogen bonding with the catalytically active Glu residues. Due to their inhibitory potency, these prismarene derivatives have been tested as pharmacological chaperones in intact cell lines from Gaucher patients carrying different mutations. The results indicated that the PrS[5]PIP is more effective toward the N370S mutation, while the DAB-1 pyrrolidine iminosugar PrS[5]PYR unexpectedly enhances L444P mutant GCase activity. This suggests that the type of iminosugar linked to the prismarene scaffold influences GCase activity rescue in a mutation-dependent manner and opens the way for the future development of increasingly efficient pharmacological chaperones.

papers.abstract_full: The iso-orbital indicator α = (τ - τvW)/τUEG is a key ingredient of meta-generalized gradient approximation (meta-GGA) functionals but diverges in low-density tails, causing unphysical exchange potentials and systematic bandgap errors as noted in Bartók and Yates [J. Chem. Phys. 150, 161101 (2019)]. We replace the denominator of α with a physically motivated Pauli kinetic energy density drawn from the orbital-free density functional theory literature, eliminating the divergence in the low density atomic tail without any empirical regularization parameter. Testing two such enhancement factors, LKT and PGS, within the r2SCAN and MS2 exchange functionals, we find that the modified indicators suppress spurious oscillations in the semilocal exchange potential and restore correct electron localization in atomic tails. For a ten-member cubic semiconductor benchmark, the bandgap mean absolute error is reduced by 41.1% for r2SCAN@PGS and 48.8% for MS2@PGS, while cohesive energy accuracy is largely preserved. The consistent improvement across two functionals with distinct constructions confirms a physical rather than functional specific origin and motivates further development of meta-GGA functionals with constraint satisfying iso-orbital indicators.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Periodontitis affects approximately 10% of the global population, posing a serious threat to tooth retention and quality of life. The disease emerges from bidirectional host-microbiome interactions that can shift from homeostasis to dysbiosis and chronic inflammation, yet conventional single-phenotype analyses cannot resolve pleiotropic loci acting across interrelated periodontal and microbial traits. We aimed to jointly model the shared genetic structure of six periodontitis-related phenotypes and to prioritise pleiotropic loci with translational relevance. METHODS AND MATERIALS: We harmonised European-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWAS) summary statistics for six traits representing host periodontal phenotypes (gingivitis, chronic periodontitis, periapical abscess, dental calculus) and oral microbial composition (genus Porphyromonas, order Bacteroidales). A common genetic factor was estimated using genomic structural equation modelling (genomic SEM), and factor-level genome-wide association analysis was conducted on 4,899,781 SNPs. The resulting signals were annotated through locus discovery and novelty assessment (FUMA), fine-mapping (SuSiE and FINEMAP), gene-level testing (MAGMA), and transcriptome-wide association with Bayesian gene prioritisation (FUSION and FOCUS). Heritability was partitioned across functional annotations (stratified LD score regression), and cell types (CELLECT); spatial enrichment was assessed using gsMap, and a polygenic risk score was constructed with PRS-CS. RESULTS: A single-factor model provided adequate fit (CFI = 1.0). Factor-level GWAS identified 127 genome-wide significant SNPs consolidating into 56 independent lead variants, all uniquely identified at the factor level. MAGMA prioritised RASAL2 and C5orf27. Fine-mapping yielded 56 variants with posterior inclusion probabilities exceeding 0.95. Transcriptome-wide association and FOCUS converged on the long non-coding RNA RP11-563N4.1 (PIP = 1). Cell-type enrichment highlighted a vascular-stromal axis led by hepatic sinusoidal endothelial cells, with additional signals in pericytes, cardiac and smooth muscle cells, endocardium, and lung stroma. Spatial mapping localised the strongest aggregate signal to lung tissue, consistent with an oral-lung mucosal axis. Polygenic risk was distributed unevenly across chromosomes. CONCLUSIONS: These analyses delineate a vascular-matrix-centred genetic architecture shared across periodontal and oral microbial traits. The prioritised loci and effector genes provide genetically informed candidates for risk stratification and for targeted investigation of periodontal pathobiology. Clinically, these genetically informed candidates may aid in identifying individuals at elevated risk and in guiding mechanism-based preventive and therapeutic strategies for periodontitis.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Cow's milk protein allergy (CMPA) affects 2-6% of children, with peak prevalence in the first year of life. Despite published guidelines, significant gaps remain in awareness and practice among healthcare providers. The aim of this study was to evaluate pediatricians' knowledge and practice styles (KPS) among pediatric care providers (PCPs) working in different Arab countries regarding their diagnosis and treatment approach to CMPA. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional multinational survey in eight Arab countries including Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Lebanon, Oman, Bahrain, United Arab Emirates (UAE), Qatar, and Kuwait. The following PCPs: pediatric specialists (PSs), pediatric residents (PRs), pediatric consultants (PCs), pediatric gastroenterologists (PGs), pediatric immunologists (PIs), general physicians (GPs), and family doctors (FDs) were included in this study. The survey was anonymous, and participants provided input on the diagnosis and management of CMPA. RESULTS: Of the 3000 questionnaires distributed to PCPs, 2145 (response rate 72%) were completed and analyzed. The majority of the respondents were male (n = 1255; 58.5%). The majority of participants were PSs (48%). Regarding the methods to diagnose CMPA, pediatricians and non-pediatricians used clinical diagnosis (61.4%), oral elimination challenge test (27.6%), specific IgE for cow's milk (8.6%) and skin prick test (1.2%) for diagnosis of CMPA ( P < 0.001). Furthermore, pediatricians used "clinical diagnosis" method to confirm CMPA significantly more than other non- pediatricians (87% vs 13%, respectively; P < 0.001). In terms of management of CMPA in breastfed infants, 67.8% reported that continuing breastfeeding with maternal elimination of cow's milk and dairy products was the best treatment approach, with significant differences between pediatricians and non-pediatricians ( P < 0.001). In terms of management of mild-moderate CMPA in formula-fed infants, hydrolyzed formula (eHF) was the most commonly prescribed (53%), while rice-based milk was the formula least often prescribed. eHF was prescribed as a first-line treatment of CMPA significantly more frequently by pediatricians than by non-pediatricians (88.9% vs 11.1%, respectively; P < 0.001). PCPs were more likely to comply (71.1%) with European Society of Pediatric Gastroenterology, Hepatology and Nutrition (ESPGHAN) clinical guidelines for CMPA. PCPs were fully agreed (68.1%) to establish unified CMPA guidelines in Arab countries. CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variability in pediatricians' KPS regarding CMPA across the participating Arab countries was identified. The identification of these gaps highlights the need for policymakers to develop educational materials for PCPs to increase their knowledge of CMPA. Evidence-based guidelines and standardized practice are needed in the Middle East.

papers.abstract_full: OBJECTIVE: "Ikigai" is a Japanese concept of meaning and purpose in life. We examined the associations of frailty and generalized trust with ikigai and their additive interaction. STUDY DESIGN: This cross-sectional study included 34,545 community-dwelling older adults (mean age 75.4 ± 6.9 years; 52.1% women) who completed postal surveys in five Japanese cities between 2019 and 2023 using the Japan Public Health Center-based Prospective Study for the Next Generation questionnaire. We created 50 imputed datasets for missing data. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: We examined associations with being without ikigai using multivariable logistic regression. We estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) using modified Poisson regression and calculated the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI). Models included city and other covariates. We also conducted a complete-case analysis. RESULTS: Overall, 74.9% of participants had ikigai. Frailty (odds ratio [OR] 3.65; 95% confidence interval [CI] 3.26-4.09) and low generalized trust (OR 2.34; 95% CI 2.22-2.47) were each associated with being without ikigai. Participants with both factors had the highest prevalence (PR 3.53; 95% CI 3.30-3.78). However, the RERI was 0.10 (95% CI -0.23 to 0.44), indicating no clear additive interaction. Complete-case findings were similar. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty and low generalized trust were each associated with being without ikigai, but no clear additive interaction was found. Longitudinal studies are needed because this cross-sectional study cannot establish causality.

papers.abstract_full: In recent years, matched plastic surgery applicants have shown a marked increase in research output, yet it remains unclear whether these academic metrics can predict the tier of the residency program into which an applicant matches. This study utilized machine learning (ML) to evaluate whether a comprehensive set of preresidency publication measures could jointly predict the matched program tier. In this retrospective, cross-sectional analysis, data were aggregated from scientific databases including PubMed and Scopus for 914 applicants who matched into ACGME-accredited integrated plastic surgery residency positions during the 2019 to 2024 National Resident Matching Program cycles. Five ML classifiers (logistic regression, decision tree, k-nearest neighbors, Gaussian naïve Bayes, and multilayer perceptron) were trained to predict program tiers under reputation-based and research-based Doximity ranking schemes. Variables included publication volume (total, first-author, and PRS-journal-specific), subspecialty categorization, and institutional variables. Performance was assessed using accuracy and F1-score (a balanced measure of precision and recall) in binary and tertiary classification settings. Performance was above chance but limited across all schemes. For binary reputation tasks, the best model achieved 61.0% accuracy and 71.4% F1-score. Under the research scheme, performance peaked at 57.5% accuracy and 66.0% F1. For tertiary classification, the best reputation result was 45% accuracy and 44% F1, and the best research result was 43% accuracy and 43% F1. No algorithm consistently outperformed the others. Preresidency publication metrics alone weakly predict the matched residency program tier, and factors beyond research output likely play a more decisive role in residency placement.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Bipolar disorder (BD) is a polygenic disease characterized by neurocognitive impairments and energy dysfunction, with potential mitochondrial involvement. We set out to examine whether mitochondrial polygenic risk scores (Mito-PRS) are associated with neurocognitive performance among youth with BD. Methods  129 youth (17.0 ± 1.9 years; n = 72 BD, n = 57 controls) completed six Cambridge Neuropsychological Test Automated Battery tasks, evaluated as a composite and independently. Mito-PRS was derived from a BD genome-wide association study and variants were selected based on their location within/near genes annotated in expertly curated mitochondrial gene databases. Associations between Mito-PRS and neurocognitive composite scores were examined in the overall sample, and within BD and controls separately. Sex-stratified analyses, mood-stratified analyses, and PRS-by-diagnosis interaction effects were also examined. All analyses controlled for age, sex, IQ, and the first two genetic principal components, and sensitivity analyses additionally controlled for psychotropic medications and mood severity. Results  Higher Mito-PRS was associated with poorer sustained attention in the overall sample (β=-0.19,  p   = 0.02) and within the BD group (β=-0.30,  p   = 0.01), but not within controls (β=-0.10,  p   = 0.44). Findings were significant in females only, and remained significant among symptomatic BD participants. Findings remained significant in sensitivity analyses. Conclusions  This study provides preliminary evidence that Mito-PRS is associated with reduced sustained attention among youth. These findings were especially salient in youth with BD and among females. While sustained attention may be specifically impacted by Mito-PRS, larger studies are warranted to examine the full spectrum of neurocognitive domains and to discern brain mechanisms underlying the observed findings.

papers.abstract_full: We identified QRSH.scwl-4B as a pleiotropic QTL for basal shoot growth and drought-stress response at the wheat germination stage, predicted its putative candidate genes, and confirmed it as a promising locus for drought-tolerance and limited yield loss. Drought stress during germination severely reduces the wheat germination rate and seedling establishment, leading to significant yield losses. Understanding the genetic control of this trait is important for breeding drought-tolerant and high-yielding wheat varieties. Here, we detected 21 quantitative trait loci (QTLs) for maximum root length (MRL), root number (RN) and shoot height (SH) under control (CK) and drought treatment (DT) at the germination stage using a recombinant inbred line (RIL) population. Among them, QSH.scwl-CK-4B, QSH.scwl-DT-4B and QRSH.scwl-4B were co-localized to a common region on chromosome arm 4BS, which exhibited pleiotropic effects on both basal shoot growth and the drought-stress response. QRSH.scwl-4B was also identified by bulked segregant analysis sequencing (BSA-Seq), mapped to a 2.09 Mb interval on 4BS, and explained 24.32%-30.89% of the phenotypic variation (PVE). Through RNA-seq, BSA-Seq and parental genome sequencing, TraesCS4B03G0104700 and TraesCS4B03G0102800 were identified as the putative candidate genes. KEGG enrichment analysis suggested that TraesCS4B03G0104700 may regulate drought tolerance during germination via jasmonic acid (JA) biosynthesis. Moreover, the positive allele of QRSH.scwl-4B increased productive tiller number (PTN) by 13.37%, while showing only limited adverse effects on other yield-related traits. This suggests that QRSH.scwl-4B is a promising locus for improving wheat drought tolerance, with potentially minimal negative impact on yield. Collectively, these findings provide a foundation for cloning QRSH.scwl-4B and for improving drought tolerance in wheat through molecular breeding.

papers.abstract_full: BACKGROUND: Relapse-like ethanol drinking behavior depends on changes in glutamate homeostasis in the mesocorticolimbic circuit. Extracellular glutamate regulation involves multiple transporters, mainly glutamate transporter 1 (GLT-1), which primarily removes the majority of extracellular glutamate; and cystine/glutamate antiporter (xCT) is co-localized with GLT-1 to be involved in this mechanism of maintaining glutamate homeostasis. AIMS: Recent studies showed that MC-100093 treatment (i.p.), a β-lactam non-antibiotic known to increase GLT-1 and xCT expression, reduced chronic ethanol consumption in male and female alcohol-preferring (P) rats. This study examined whether MC-100093 may reduce relapse-like ethanol drinking behavior. METHODS: P rats (both male and female) had access to 15% and 30% ethanol and water for 5 weeks and were treated with MC-100093 (100 mg/kg, i.p.) during the last 4 days of a 1-week deprivation period (week 6), continuing into 3 days of re-exposure (week 7). RESULTS: MC-100093-treated rats exhibited lower ethanol intake and preference during re-exposure compared to saline-treated groups, across sexes. Additionally, MC-100093 treatment showed a sex difference in ethanol intake and preference after re-exposure. Moreover, MC-100093 attenuated ethanol-induced downregulation of GLT-1 and xCT expression in the medial prefrontal cortex (Prelimbic, PL; and Infralimbic, IL) and nucleus accumbens (core and shell) regions. Importantly, MC-100093 did not affect rat body weights. CONCLUSIONS: These results report for the first time the efficacy of GLT-1 modulator, MC-100093, on attenuating relapse-like ethanol drinking behaviors.

papers.abstract_full: Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus (S. zooepidemicus) is a zoonotic pathogen affecting various mammals, yet its genomic epidemiology remains poorly understood. To address this, we analyzed 428 S. zooepidemicus strains from six countries (1993-2024). The whole-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) revealed four clades, with genetic diversity driven by lineage rather than host species or geographic origin. The findings support the conclusion that S. zooepidemicus is a host generalist, with horses serving as the primary host. The identified virulence-associated genes (VAGs) showed clade-specific distribution patterns: clade 1 lacked adherence factor genes srtC.2/3/4, clade 2 was enriched for the IgG-degrading enzyme gene ideZ, and clade 4 was enriched for a specific allele of the virulence-associated coupling protein gene virD4. Antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) were detected in 18.2% of strains, and no multidrug resistance was found. ARG prevalence was associated with clade 4, with tetracycline resistance being the most common. Mobile genetic elements (MGEs) are pivotal in shaping the accessory genome profiles: prophages function as the primary carriers of exotoxin genes, while integrative and conjugative elements (ICEs) serve as the main vehicles for ARGs. Notably, the co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs was identified on ICESz1, predominantly in clade 4 isolates. In conclusion, the pathogenic potential and resistance profiles of S. zooepidemicus are shaped by specific evolutionary lineages driven by MGEs. These elements act not only as genetic cargo but also as drivers that provide the conjugative machinery to co-disseminate virulence and resistance traits, accelerating the evolution of zoonotic lineages.IMPORTANCES. zooepidemicus is an opportunistic pathogen capable of infecting a wide range of hosts, including humans, often causing severe diseases. This study provides a framework for understanding the evolution of S. zooepidemicus, highlighting that its pathogenic potential and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) profiles are shaped by specific MGE-driven evolutionary lineages. The co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs on ICEs indicates that these elements provide both the pathogenic advantage and the conjugative machinery required for horizontal spread in S. zooepidemicus. This suggests that antibiotic selection can promote the transmission of virulent S. zooepidemicus lineages. These findings underscore the need for integrated surveillance strategies to monitor both virulence and AMR traits in S. zooepidemicus within equine populations to benefit public health.

Notably, the co-localization of the invasion-associated virD4 allele and ARGs was identified on ICESz1, predominantly in clade 4 isolates.
In conclusion, the pathogenic potential and resistance profiles of S. zooepidemicus are shaped by specific evolutionary lineages driven by MGEs.

papers.abstract_full: PR-toxin and Sporogen-AO1 have garnered widespread interest, and their structural divergence is attributed to two distinctive sets of tailoring enzymes. Despite recent elucidation of their respective biosynthetic pathways, these two distinctive tailoring cassettes can only operate independently within natural hosts. Based on the Characteristic Post-Modification Colocalization genome mining strategy, this study reports the first discovery of a new class of biosynthetic gene clusters with merged characteristic post-modifications. Furthermore, heterologous expression of pbe gene cluster, led to the production of seven new eremophilane-type sesquiterpenoids (1-7). Notably, compound 1 represents the first occurring eremophilane-type sesquiterpene bearing both 1,2-epoxy and 6,7-epoxy moieties. In bioassays, compounds 3 and 8 exhibited significant cytotoxicity against the K562 cell line, with IC50 values of 10.93 μM and 1.03 μM, respectively. Taken together, this research offers an innovative method for the directed discovery of natural products.

papers.abstract_full: AIMS: Spatially resolved omics technologies enable investigation of cellular interactions within their local microenvironments (neighbourhoods) directly in situ. Although several computational methods have been developed for neighbourhood analysis, significant limitations remain in how neighbourhoods are defined and interrogated. Here, we present Kandinsky, a toolkit that provides a flexible and versatile framework for defining and analysing cell neighbourhoods. METHODS: We developed Kandinsky to improve flexibility in neighbourhood analysis and maximise compatibility with a wide range of spatial omics data. We therefore implemented multiple approaches for identifying cell- or spot-based neighbourhoods that serve as input for four analytical modules: differential gene or protein expression analysis, neighbourhood clustering, co-localisation/dispersion, and spatial hot and cold areas. In addition to its core functionality, Kandinsky enables the execution of external tools within the same analytical framework. RESULTS: We applied Kandinsky to real and simulated spatial datasets to benchmark its performance against existing methods and demonstrate its ability to uncover biologically meaningful spatial interactions. Kandinsky achieved competitive performance in terms of accuracy, memory usage, and runtime. In real datasets, it suggested transcriptional changes associated with acinar-to-beta cell reprogramming in the healthy pancreas; recapitulated stromal, immune, and tumour-associated clusters in pancreatic cancer; revealed the spatial co-localisation of myoepithelial cells with specific breast cancer subpopulations; and confirmed the association between regions of high CD74 expression and immune cell infiltration. CONCLUSION: Kandinsky is a flexible and versatile toolkit for neighbourhood analysis that facilitates the exploration and interpretation of complex spatial omics data.

papers.abstract_full: PURPOSE: Anemia is a recognized complication of hypothyroidism, but disease-level genetic studies have not identified a clear erythroid cell-intrinsic target. We integrated genetic validation, molecular-QTL prioritization, and replicated triiodothyronine (T3)-responsive erythroid experiments to identify candidates linking hypothyroidism liability to anemia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) assessed genetically predicted hypothyroidism and anemia. Source metadata were reviewed for possible sample overlap, and two cross-biobank forward validations were performed. Strict reverse MR used the original OpenGWAS identifiers; because anemia provided no genome-wide-significant instruments, a post hoc analysis used p < 5 × 10-6. Non-major histocompatibility complex (MHC) methylation summary-based Mendelian randomization (SMR) and whole-blood expression SMR were integrated, followed by a public fine-mapping/colocalization lookup for two acyl-CoA synthetase long-chain family member 5 (ACSL5) cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG) sites and the ACSL5 eQTL. ACSL5 was examined in three independent hemin-induced K562, a human chronic myelogenous leukemia cell line experiments with or without T3; Triacsin C and oleic acid-bovine serum albumin (BSA) served as pathway-level perturbations. RESULTS: Primary inverse-variance weighted (IVW) analysis associated hypothyroidism liability with higher anemia odds (OR = 1.0304; 95% CI, 1.0195-1.0414; p = 3.42 × 10-8). Both primary genome-wide association studies (GWASs) were UK Biobank-derived, and their exact participant overlap could not be determined from public summary-level information. A participant-independent FinnGen hypothyroidism-to-UK Biobank anemia validation reproduced the positive direction (28 instruments; IVW beta = 0.001448, p = 4.14 × 10-4); the complementary UK Biobank hypothyroidism-to-FinnGen anemia analysis was also positive. Strict original-ID reverse MR was not estimable; the exploratory eight-instrument analysis was null and heterogeneous. Six non-MHC CpGs passed Bonferroni correction, including two mapped to ACSL5, while whole-blood ACSL5 expression showed an inverse SMR estimate. The public lookup returned no pairwise CpG-expression colocalization. In all three K562 experiments, hemin plus T3 increased HBA1, HBA2, GYPA, and ACSL5 expression. Triacsin C suppressed erythroid-marker expression, whereas oleic acid-BSA produced a partial increase without exogenous T3. CONCLUSION: Cross-scale evidence prioritizes ACSL5 as a T3-responsive candidate linking hypothyroidism liability to anemia and implicates long-chain fatty-acid handling as a research direction. However, negative CpG-expression colocalization and nongene-specific pharmacological interventions preclude a mechanistic conclusion. Direct ACSL5 perturbation and primary erythroid-cell validation are required.

papers.abstract_full: Nuclear pore complexes (NPCs) are nuclear envelope (NE)-embedded protein assemblies that mediate nucleocytoplasmic exchange and interact with the genome, including binding of an NPC component Nup93 to Polycomb chromatin domains. Here, we investigated the in vivo relevance of this relationship in Drosophila, which unusually contains two distinct paralogs of Nup93. Interestingly, we identified a Nup93-2-specific tumorigenic phenotype in larval wings, where depletion of Nup93-2, but not Nup93-1, led to tumor-like overgrowth, reminiscent of Polycomb mutations. Consistently, our transcriptomic analysis revealed a wide-spread loss of gene silencing in Nup93-2-depleted wings, particularly in a Nup93-bound Polycomb domain spanning genes for activators of JAK/STAT signaling. Nup93 paralogs were not found to differ in their effect on NPC biogenesis but strikingly, showed differences in subnuclear localization patterns. While Nup93-1 co-localized exclusively with fully assembled NPCs, Nup93-2 exhibited only partial co-localization and was found at additional NE locations in a tissue-specific manner. Together, our results identify an in vivo silencing role of a Nup93 paralog and suggest that Nup93-2 may form a unique NE-associated complex that targets a subset of Polycomb domains containing growth-promoting genes.

papers.abstract_full: Annexins (ANNs) are Ca2+-dependent phospholipid-binding proteins that play important roles in plant responses to environmental stress. However, the apple ANN gene family and the regulatory mechanisms by which ANNs participate in cold-stress responses remain poorly understood. In this study, 15 MdANN family members were identified in the apple genome and divided into three subfamilies. Among them, MdANN2 expression was strongly induced by low temperature. Functional analyses showed that MdANN2 overexpression markedly enhanced cold tolerance in apple, whereas virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) of MdANN2 compromised cold tolerance. Subcellular localization assays revealed that MdANN2 localized to the plasma membrane, cytoplasm, and nucleus. Non-invasive micro-test technology (NMT) further showed that MdANN2 is associated with Ca2+-permeable channel activity: cold stimulation significantly enhanced cytosolic Ca2+ influx in MdANN2-overexpressing plants, whereas exogenous application of the Ca2+ channel blocker LaCl3 or the Ca2+ chelator EGTA substantially inhibited this influx. The kinases MdMPK6a and MdMPK6b physically interacted with and phosphorylated MdANN2 both in vitro and in vivo. Silencing MdMPK6a/b significantly increased apple cold tolerance, whereas overexpression of MdMPK6a/b reduced apple cold tolerance. Moreover, transient overexpression of MdMPK6a/b in the MdANN2-overexpression background attenuated MdANN2-mediated cold tolerance and Ca2+ influx. In addition, co-localization assays showed that MdMPK6a/b decreased the accumulation of MdANN2 at the plasma membrane. Together, these findings demonstrate that MdANN2 positively regulates apple cold tolerance by promoting cold-induced Ca2+ influx, a process inhibited by MdMPK6a/b-mediated phosphorylation. This study identifies a novel MdMPK6a/b-MdANN2 module that governs Ca2+ signaling in apple under cold stress, thereby providing promising molecular targets for improving cold tolerance in apple and other crop species.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Introduction  The difficulty of identifying and describing feelings (alexithymia) has been associated with problematic coping strategies (e.g. drinking) in college students. Expanding on prior work, the present study explored whether a novel two-week Somatic Avatar (SA) training would improve emotion regulation in college students and if the effect differed between students with varied levels of alexithymia. Method  Sixteen college students (  M  age  = 22.88; 81% non-Hispanic White) completed a two-week protocol that entailed four days of yoga training paired with three days of processing an individualized and animated avatar of their yoga practice. Participants completed demographic questions, the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness scale (MAIA-2), and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale – 20 (TAS – 20) at baseline. They also completed baseline and exit assessments of the Distress Tolerance Scale (DTS). Median split groupings fell naturally in the moderate and high ranges of the TAS-20. Findings  After controlling for interoception, a mixed-model analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) showed a significant effect of alexithymia on distress tolerance change scores from pre- to post- SA training, with participants endorsing moderate alexithymia (  p  = .006) demonstrating greater improvement in distress tolerance than participants with high alexithymia (  p  = .589),  F  (1, 13) = 6.346,  p  = .026, partial η2 = .328. Discussion  Results suggested that the novel SA training may improve distress tolerance in those who struggle to identify their emotions. Future research should experimentally manipulate the length of training and increase the sample size to assess the effects of training among individuals with high alexithymia.

papers.abstract_full: Abstract    Background  Amyloid-β (Aβ) pathology in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) includes distinct types of plaques and cerebral amyloid angiopathy (CAA). Post-translational modifications (PTMs) may define Aβ deposit-specific signatures. Among them, nitration of tyrosine-10 (3′-nitrotyrosine, 3-NT) links oxidative stress to Aβ modification and microglial activation, but its spatial distribution across deposit types and impact on aggregation dynamics remain unclear. Methods  Parietal cortex tissue from AD and CAA cases (n = 19) and controls (n = 9) was analyzed by multiplex immunofluorescence for Aβ species (Aβaa1-8, AβN3pE, pSer8-Aβ), 3-NT, thioflavin-S, and CD68. Distinct deposits, including diffuse plaques (n = 70) classic cored plaques (n = 70), coarse-grained plaques (n = 40), capillary CAA (capCAA; n = 80), larger vessel CAA (n = 80), and leptomeningeal CAA (n = 25) were annotated, together with gray matter regions from control tissue lacking Aβ pathology (n = 90). In vitro assays evaluated how 3-NT affects Aβ aggregation kinetics, microglial morphology, and neuronal viability. Results  We observed Aβ deposit-specific PTM signatures. Classic cored and coarse-grained plaques contained increased pyroglutamylated (Aβ  N3pE  ) and phosphorylated (pSer8-Aβ) species compared to diffuse plaques. In contrast, 3-NT showed a distinct vascular predilection, with the highest relative burden in larger vessel and leptomeningeal CAA. 3-NT colocalized with β-sheet–rich thioflavin-S-positive fibrils and areas of CD68-positive microglia. In vitro, nitration slowed oligomer-to-fibril conversion but accelerated the growth of pre-formed fibrils and sustained microglial activation without increasing neuronal toxicity. Conclusions  Distinct PTMs delineate the compartment-specific architectural signatures of Aβ deposits. Whereas AβN3pE and pSer8-Aβ broadly label parenchymal plaques, 3-NT shows a vascular predilection, particularly in leptomeningeal CAA. This compartmentalized pattern identifies nitration as a candidate marker of vascular Aβ pathology and a possible risk indicator for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during anti-Aβ immunotherapy.

papers.abstract_full: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is a distinct myocardial disease defined by the existence of abnormal myocardial structure and performance in diabetes mellitus patients without hypertension and coronary artery disease. DCM has been identified as a major cause of heart failure, hospitalisation and cardiovascular mortality with increasing global burden of diabetes. However, there is a large interindividual variation in disease susceptibility, disease progression and response to therapy, highlighting the limitations of conventional management strategies that are applied uniformly. Precision medicine provides a transformational approach through the integration of genomic, molecular, imaging, clinical and lifestyle data to allow for personalized risk assessment, early diagnosis, prognostication and treatment. This review presents the recent advances in the field of precision medicine for DCM with a focus on the molecular pathological mechanisms including metabolic disorders, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, fibrosis and microvascular injury. We discuss the relevance of genomics, pharmacogenomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, lipidomics and epigenomics in the context of disease heterogeneity and identification of novel therapeutic targets. Emerging biomarkers including circulating microRNAs, non-coding RNAs, inflammatory mediators, fibrosis-related markers and extracellular vesicles are discussed for their potential in personal diagnosis and prognosis. We also consider the increasing role of advanced cardiac imaging, digital phenotyping, wearable technologies, artificial intelligence, and machine learning in enhancing early detection and clinical decision-making. In this review, the therapeutic advances, including sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists, anti-fibrotic therapies, mitochondrial-targeted interventions, regenerative medicine, gene therapy, and RNA-based therapeutics, are discussed, with a focus on the precision medicine approach. Finally, we present current challenges in data integration, clinical validation, cost-effectiveness, and ethical issues, and highlight future directions in digital twins, multi-omics integration, and AI-driven personalized cardiology. The combination of these technologies has the potential to revolutionize the prevention and management of diabetic cardiomyopathy and improve cardiovascular outcomes in patients with diabetes.
